llm.summary: This is a focused markdown-only sales architecture proposal skill with disclosed web research, no code execution, persistence, credential access, or hidden behavior.

dimensions.detail: Requested environment use is proportionate to the purpose: web search for public customer and industry context, with no local file indexing or system access requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, executable script, dependency, remote payload, or package setup was present; the artifact is a single markdown instruction file.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a Chinese executive-style deliverable and online research; this is visible in the artifact, though users should avoid entering confidential customer details if web search will be used.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, background process, memory writes, credential use, or tool hijacking instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities fit its stated purpose: it asks the agent to use user-provided customer context and online search to draft a B2B cloud digital transformation proposal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before using this skill, avoid pasting confidential customer architecture, nonpublic pain points, or sensitive commercial details unless you are comfortable with the agent using them to form web searches. For public-account planning and Chinese executive proposals, the behavior is coherent and low risk.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The web-search concern is valid as privacy guidance: the skill does not include consent or query minimization language. However, online research is explicitly disclosed and directly supports the proposal-writing purpose, so this does not make the artifact suspicious by itself.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language output requirement is a usability/localization constraint, not evidence of security risk or hidden behavior.
